images.title: Removed twice, so add 12 back
images.purpose: Shows (a − 3)(b − 4) with a = b = 10: removing 4 columns and 3 rows from a 10 by 10 square takes the 3 by 4 corner away twice, so +12 comes back.
images.composition: One large square grid of cells centred, with its right columns and bottom rows coloured differently. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: A 10 by 10 grid of equal square cells, 100 cells. The top left block of 7 rows by 6 columns (42 cells) is teal (#0072B2). The right strip of 4 columns in the top 7 rows (28 cells) and the bottom strip of 3 rows in the left 6 columns (18 cells) are pale vermilion (#D55E00) with thin diagonal hatching. The bottom right block of 3 rows by 4 columns (12 cells) is reddish purple (#CC79A7). Above the grid the label '100' at the top left corner; a thin grey bracket over the 4 right columns with the label '− 40'; a thin grey bracket beside the 3 bottom rows on the left with the label '− 30'. The label '+ 12' on the purple block, with 'removed twice' just below the grid under it. The label '7 × 6 = 42' on the teal block. Exactly 100 cells: 42 teal, 46 hatched, 12 purple.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Taking away 3 rows and 4 columns removes the corner twice, so (−3) × (−4) = +12.
images.description: Shows (a − 3)(b − 4) with a = b = 10: removing 4 columns and 3 rows from a 10 by 10 square takes the 3 by 4 corner away twice, so +12 comes back.

image_decisions.why: The positive last term is the hard part; the overlap picture shows where +12 comes from.
